newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Russian, Belarus diplomats deny N.Y. police charges.
newsitem.headline: Russian, Belarus diplomats deny N.Y. police charges.

text.p: A Russian diplomat with an arm in a cast and a sling, and a colleague from Belarus, denied on Tuesday they were drunk or threw any punches during a fracas with New York police that has escalated into an international incident.

Boris Obnossov, a 43-year-old first secretary with Russia's U.N. mission, and Yuri Orange, 50, a first secretary at the Belarus mission, gave their account of the Dec. 29 incident that led to a demand by New York Mayor Rudolph Giuliani for their recall.
The two men's ambassadors have written to the U.S. State Department demanding official explanations and an apology, as well as compensation for damages sustained by Obnossov.

Police say two officers pulled Obnossov from a car in which the diplomats were seated because he appeared intoxicated after parking illegally near a fire hydrant. They said Orange then punched one of the officers.
The U.N. committee on relations with the host country will discuss the incident at a meeting requested by Russian U.N. ambassador Sergei Lavrov.

"When I produced my diplomatic ID, the officer threw it on the floor of my car," Obnossov told a news conference at the Russian U.N. mission on what, according to the Russian Orthodox calendar, was Christmas Day.
"When I tried to pick it up, he dragged me out. When I fell on the ground and he twisted my hand, as a result I lost my consciousness," Obnossov added.
"I never resisted any law enforcement action. Even in this case I did not resist at all," he told a questioner.
Orange said he was pulled from the car "without any reasons ... after I had twice showed ... my diplomatic identification."

He said one of the officers was "rude, aggressive and nervously unstable." When asked his name, he replied: "John Smith," Orange said. The police officers were also alleged to have cursed the diplomats and their countries.
Denying they were drunk, Obnossov said he had had "maybe one glass of dry wine" during lunch at a nearby Chinese restaurant. Orange said he drank nothing.

The Russian mission's press counsellor, Evgeny Menkes, who conducted the news conference with his Belarus counterpart, Alyaksei Skrypko, said it seemed "fairly strange" that when the two men were taken to a police station they were not tested for alcohol.
And when they left, Orange was permitted to drive the car since Obnossov's injury prevented him from doing so.

Asked whether he had received 386 parking tickets last year, Obnossov said this was "approximately the right figure," volunteering that he had received up to eight tickets in a single day. But this was because the Russian U.N. mission had only 10 parking places for more than 100 cars, he said.
The parking ticket issue was another source of Mayor Giuliani's ire and he has demanded tens of thousands of dollars in unpaid fines, though diplomats are immune from prosecution.
